definition: For each product with at least 20 days of price coverage in both months, we take its median daily price in the month and compare it with its own median daily price in the same month a year earlier; the figure is the median of those per-product changes.
note: Frozen monthly records for the MemRadar Memory Price Index. APPEND ONLY. A record is written once and never recomputed; a later correction appends to corrections[] and carries its own complete replacement record inline, pairs included. Version 1 supports inline replacement records only. Written by scripts/build-price-index-archive.js (the one-time launch backfill) and by the monthly freeze in scripts/generate-product-pages.js. Do not hand-edit.
caveats: SURVIVORSHIP. The tracked catalogue was assembled on 2026-07-22, so every historical record describes products still sold in July 2026. Products discontinued before then are absent and always will be.

CHANGE POINTS, NOT DAILY READINGS. Before 2026-07-22 the stored history is a one-time Keepa load of price change points. The carried-forward monthly price reconstructs the full month from them; it is a reconstruction, and figures here will not reconcile exactly with the raw-readings monthly CSV.

MISSING-ASIN AMBIGUITY. Before the missing-ASIN logging code was committed to backend/lib/priceFetch.js on 2026-10-12, Keepa omitting an ASIN from a response cannot be told apart from a null price in stored data, because both produce an absence in a run that concluded success. Records whose months fall before that date carry that ambiguity. Its measured bound: 203 of 235 products were never absent, 99.3% of absence sat in runs of two or more consecutive batches, and for the one batch where a direct cross-check was possible the absent set and the retailer_offers out-of-stock set matched exactly, 16 of 16.

rule.no_offer_backfill: Before 2026-07-22 the history is a one-time Keepa load whose csv is a change-point series, so a price_history row with in_stock=false marks the START of a no-offer interval that ends at the next in-stock row, not a single bad day (scripts/backfill-keepa.js:45-61).
rule.no_offer_live: From 2026-07-22, a successful fetch writes one price_history row per in-stock product and no row at all when the product has no offer (backend/lib/priceFetch.js:190-205), so there are zero in_stock=false rows in the live era. A fetch batch is therefore identified by a distinct price_history.fetched_at value, which the fetch stamps once per run and shares across every row it writes (backend/lib/priceFetch.js:178). A UTC day on which at least one batch exists and on which the product appears in NONE of that day's batches is treated as an observed no-offer day. A day on which the product appears in at least one batch is covered, even if it is absent from another batch the same day. A day with no batch at all is not evidence either way and leaves the carry running. This rule is evaluated from price_history alone and uses no current-state table.

rule.median_helper: median(xs) in backend/lib/stats.js, even n is the mean of the two middle values

rule.no_offer_live: From 2026-07-22, a successful fetch writes one price_history row per in-stock product and no row at all when the product has no offer (backend/lib/priceFetch.js:190-205), so there are zero in_stock=false rows in the live era. A fetch batch is therefore identified by a distinct price_history.fetched_at value, which the fetch stamps once per run and shares across every row it writes (backend/lib/priceFetch.js:178). A UTC day on which at least one batch exists and on which the product appears in NONE of that day's batches is treated as an observed no-offer day. A day on which the product appears in at least one batch is covered, even if it is absent from another batch the same day. A day with no batch at all is not evidence either way and leaves the carry running. This rule is evaluated from price_history alone and uses no current-state table.
